bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷五 梁書5: 太祖本紀五
title.en: Volume 5 Book of Later Liang 5: Taizu Annals 5
title.raw: 卷五 梁書5: 太祖本紀五 Volume 5 Book of Later Liang 5: Taizu Annals 5

sentences.zh: 開平三年九月癸巳朔，御崇勳殿，宴群臣文武百官。

translations.literal: On guisi, first day of the ninth month of Kaiping 3, the Emperor presided at Chongxun Hall and feasted the civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the first of the ninth month of Kaiping 3, the Emperor held court at Chongxun Hall and feasted chief ministers and the full civil and military establishment.

sentences.zh: 賜張宗奭、楊師厚白綾各三百匹，銀鞍轡馬。

translations.literal: He granted Zhang Zongshi and Yang Shihou each three hundred bolts of white silk and horses with silver saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhang Zongshi and Yang Shihou each three hundred bolts of white silk and horses fitted with silver saddles and bridles.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上幸崇政院宴內臣，賜院使敬翔、直學士李班等繒彩有差。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Emperor visited Chongzheng Academy to feast the inner attendants, granting silks in varying amounts to academy director Jing Xiang, direct academician Li Ban, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he visited Chongzheng Academy to feast the inner attendants, granting graded gifts of silks to director Jing Xiang, direct academician Li Ban, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎、平章事薛貽矩判建昌宮事，兼延資庫使。

translations.literal: Vice director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor Xue Yiju was assigned to administer Jianchang Palace affairs and concurrently made commissioner of the Yanzi Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju, vice director of the Chancellery and grand councilor, was put in charge of Jianchang Palace and named commissioner of the Yanzi Treasury as well.

sentences.zh: 制：「內外使臣復命，未見便歸私第者，朝廷命使，臣下奉行，惟於辭見之儀，合守敬恭之道。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "When internal and external envoys report back, those who return to private residences without having been received—court orders are issued and subjects obey; only in the rites of leave-taking and audience should the path of reverence be observed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Envoys from within and without who report back must not go home before they have been received. The court issues orders and subjects obey; only in the ceremonies of farewell and audience is reverence required.

sentences.zh: 近者凡差出使，往復皆越常規。

translations.literal: Recently all who are dispatched on mission, coming and going, have exceeded proper practice.
translations.idiomatic: Lately every envoy sent out has broken routine on the journey there and back.

sentences.zh: 或已辭而尚在本家，或未見而先歸私第，但從己便，莫稟王程。

translations.literal: Some have taken leave but still remain at home; some return to private residences before having been received—they follow their own convenience and do not respect the royal schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Some have bowed out yet still stay at home; some reach their own houses before an audience—each does as he pleases and ignores the imperial timetable.

sentences.zh: 在禮敬而殊乖，置典章而私舉。

translations.literal: This is contrary to ritual propriety, setting aside statutes for private conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual terms it is deeply wrong; in law they set aside the code for private convenience.

sentences.zh: 宜令御史臺別具條流事件具黜罰等奏聞。

translations.literal: The Censorate should separately set forth articles on particular instances of dismissal and punishment and submit a report.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate should draw up detailed rules on offenses and penalties and memorialize them.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，殿直王唐福自襄城走馬，以天軍勝捷逆將李洪歸降事上聞。

translations.literal: " On gengzi Palace Guard Wang Tangfu rode post from Xiangcheng to report that the imperial army had won a victory and that the rebel leader Li Hong had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengzi Palace Guard Wang Tangfu galloped from Xiangcheng with word that the imperial army had won and the rebel Li Hong had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賜唐福絹銀有加，宰臣百官上表稱賀。

translations.literal: Tangfu was granted additional silk and silver; chief ministers and officials submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Tangfu received extra silk and silver; chief ministers and officials submitted felicitations.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，開封府虞候李繼業齎襄州都指揮使程暉奏狀，以今月五日，殺戮逆黨千人，並生擒都指揮使傅霸以下節級共五百人，收復襄州人戶歸業事。

translations.literal: On renyin Kaifeng Prefecture patrol officer Li Jiye presented a memorial from Xiangzhou commander Cheng Hui stating that on the fifth of this month they killed a thousand rebels, captured over five hundred including military commissioner Fu Ba and those of command rank, and restored Xiangzhou households to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Li Jiye of Kaifeng Prefecture patrol delivered Cheng Hui’s report from Xiangzhou: on the fifth they had slain a thousand rebels, taken Fu Ba and some five hundred officers of command rank alive, and brought the people of Xiangzhou back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：八月，陳暉軍至襄州，李洪逆戰，大敗，王求死。

translations.literal: 《Zizhi Tongjian》: In the eighth month Chen Hui’s army reached Xiangzhou; Li Hong fought in reverse and was greatly defeated; Wang Qiu died.
translations.idiomatic: 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: In the eighth month Chen Hui reached Xiangzhou; Li Hong gave battle and was routed; Wang Qiu was killed.

sentences.zh: 九月丁酉，拔其城，斬叛兵千人，執李洪、楊虔等送洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: On the ninth month’s dingyou they took the city, beheaded a thousand mutinous troops, seized Li Hong, Yang Qian, and others and sent them to Luoyang for execution.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the ninth month the city fell; a thousand mutineers were beheaded and Li Hong, Yang Qian, and the rest were sent to Luoyang and executed.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝御文明殿，以收復襄漢，受宰臣以下稱賀。

translations.literal: On guimao the Emperor presided at Wuming Hall to receive congratulations from chief ministers and below on the recovery of Xiang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Emperor took the hall at Wuming and accepted congratulations from the chief ministers down on recovering Xiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，侍中韓建罷守太保，左僕射、同平章事楊涉罷守本官，乙太常卿趙光逢為中書侍郎、平章事，翰林學士奉旨、工部侍郎、知制誥杜曉為尚書戶部侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: On xinhai Chief Minister Han Jian was relieved to Grand Preceptor; Left Vice Director and Co-Grand Councilor Yang She was relieved to his original post; Zhao Guangfeng, grand master of splendid happiness, was made vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor; Du Xiao, drafting academician, vice minister of works, and edict drafter, was made vice director of the Revenue Ministry and grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Han Jian stepped down as chief minister to Grand Preceptor; Yang She, left vice director and co-grand councilor, returned to his former post; Zhao Guangfeng became vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor; Du Xiao, drafting Hanlin academician and vice minister of works, became vice director of the Revenue Ministry and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「秋冬之際，陰雨相仍，所司擇日拜郊，或慮臨時妨事，宜令別更擇日奏聞。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "In the autumn-winter season rain follows rain; the offices have chosen a day for the suburban sacrifice, yet we fear last-minute hindrance—another day should be chosen and reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Autumn and winter bring unbroken rain; though a suburban date has been chosen, it may yet be disrupted—select another day and report.

sentences.zh: 」是月，禮儀使奏：「據所司擇，十月二日，祀圓丘。

translations.literal: " That month the Ritual Commissioner memorialized: "According to the offices’ selection, the second of the tenth month is set for sacrifice at the Round Altar.
translations.idiomatic: " That month the ritual commissioner reported: "The offices propose the second of the tenth month for the Round Altar sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今參詳十月十七日以後入十一月節，十一月二日冬至一陽生之辰，宜行親告之禮。

translations.literal: Now on review, after the seventeenth of the tenth month we enter the eleventh month; on the eleventh month’s second day—the winter solstice, the day yang first arises—the personal announcement rite should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: On review, after the seventeenth of the tenth month we enter the eleventh month; on its second day, the winter solstice when yang is reborn, the Emperor should perform the personal announcement rite instead.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 河中奏，准宣，詔使有銅牌者，所至即易騎以遣。

translations.literal: Hezhong reported that per edict, envoys bearing bronze tallies should have horses exchanged wherever they arrive for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong reported that per imperial order, envoys with bronze tallies were to have mounts changed at each post for rapid relay.

sentences.zh: 十月癸未，大明節，帝御文明殿，設齋僧道，召宰臣、翰林學士預之，諸道節度、刺史及內外諸司使咸有進獻。

translations.literal: On guiwei of the tenth month, the Grand Brightness festival, the Emperor presided at Wuming Hall, set out vegetarian offerings for monks and Daoists, summoned chief ministers and Hanlin academicians, and military governors, prefects, and commissioners within and without all presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Grand Brightness festival in the tenth month, the Emperor held Wuming Hall, fed monks and Daoists, and called in chief ministers and Hanlin scholars; governors, prefects, and commissioners from within and without all brought gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔以寇盜未平，凡諸給過所，並令司門郎中、員外郎出給，以杜奸詐。

translations.literal: An edict directed that because bandits were not yet pacified, all travel permits should be issued by directors and vice directors of the Gate Office to prevent fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Because rebels still roamed, an edict required that all travel passes be issued only by directors and vice directors of the Gate Office to block forgery.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸已朔，帝齋於內殿，不視朝。

translations.literal: On guisi, first day of the eleventh month, the Emperor fasted in the inner palace and held no court.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the first of the eleventh month, he fasted in the inner palace and held no audience.

sentences.zh: 甲午，日長至，五更一點自大內出，于文明殿受宰臣以下起居，自五鳳樓出南郊，左右金吾、太常、兵部等司儀仗法駕鹵簿及左右內直控鶴等引從赴壇，文武百官太保韓建以下班以候，帝升壇告謝。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the day the sun reached its utmost length, at fifth watch first mark he emerged from the inner palace, at Wuming Hall received the obeisance of chief ministers and below, then from Wufeng Tower went out to the southern suburb; the Left and Right Golden Guard, Directorate of Imperial Music, Ministry of War, and others with regalia and inner-palace crane riders escorted him to the altar; civil and military officials including Grand Preceptor Han Jian awaited in formation; the Emperor ascended the altar to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the winter solstice, at the first mark of fifth watch he left the inner palace, took obeisance from the chief ministers at Wuming Hall, then went south from Wufeng Tower with Golden Guard, music directorate, war ministry, full regalia, and inner crane riders to the altar where Han Jian and the officials stood in ranks; the Emperor mounted and gave thanks.

sentences.zh: 司天臺奏：冬至日，自夜半後，祥風微扇，帝座澄明，至曉，黃雲捧日。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Bureau reported: On the solstice, from after midnight a propitious breeze stirred mildly, the celestial throne seat was clear, and at dawn yellow clouds embraced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau reported: After midnight on the solstice a lucky wind breathed lightly, the sky over the throne was bright, and at dawn yellow clouds cupped the sun.

sentences.zh: 丙申，畋於上東門外。

translations.literal: On bingshen he hunted outside the Upper East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he hunted beyond the Upper East Gate.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，制曰：

translations.literal: On wuxu an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 夫嚴親報本，所以通神明；

translations.literal: Honoring close kin and repaying origins is how one communicates with the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: To honor kin and repay origins is to reach the spirits;

sentences.zh: 流澤覃休，所以惠黎庶。

translations.literal: Extending grace and spreading blessing is how one benefits the people.
translations.idiomatic: to spread blessing is to succor the people.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋邦家不易之道，皇王自昔之規，敢斁大猷，茲惟古義。

translations.literal: These are unchanging principles of state and rules of kings from antiquity—I dare not violate this great design, for it is the ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the unchanging ways of empire and the measure of kings since old—I dare not slight this great pattern; it is the ancient duty.

sentences.zh: 粵朕受命，於今三年，何曾不寅畏晨興，焦勞夕惕。

translations.literal: Since receiving the Mandate, three years have passed—when have I not risen early in reverent caution and toiled evening and night?
translations.idiomatic: From the day I received the Mandate three years have passed—when have I not risen before dawn in awe and labored far into the night?

sentences.zh: 師唐、虞之典，上則於乾功，挹殷、夏之源，下涵於民極。

translations.literal: Taking Tang and Yu as models above to align with heavenly achievement, drawing from Yin and Xia sources below to encompass the people’s pole—
translations.idiomatic: I take Tang and Yu as my pattern above to match Heaven’s work and draw on Yin and Xia below to hold up the people’s foundation—

sentences.zh: 欲使萬方有裕，六辨無愆。

translations.literal: I wish all within the four seas to have plenty and the six duties to be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: that all under Heaven may prosper and the six ministries keep their measure.

sentences.zh: 然而志有所未孚，理有所未達，致奸宄作釁，旱霪為災。

translations.literal: Yet intentions are not fully realized and principle is not fully attained, causing traitors to raise disturbances and drought and flood to become disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my will is not wholly trusted nor principle wholly reached—traitors make war and drought and flood scour the land.

sentences.zh: 驕將守邊，擁牙旗而背義；

translations.literal: Arrogant generals hold the frontier, bearing military banners in defiance of duty;
translations.idiomatic: Proud commanders on the border fly their banners against their oath;

sentences.zh: 積陰馭氣，陵玉燭以幹和。

translations.literal: accumulated yin dominates qi, assaulting the jade candle and disturbing harmony.
translations.idiomatic: yin masses and rides the qi, striking at the jade candle of harmony.

sentences.zh: 載考休征，式昭至警。

translations.literal: Examining these signs reveals the utmost warning.
translations.idiomatic: Reading these omens shows the gravest warning.

sentences.zh: 朕是以仰高俯厚，靡惜於責躬；

translations.literal: Therefore I look up high and down low, sparing nothing in self-reproach;
translations.idiomatic: So I look up to Heaven and down to earth and spare nothing in blaming myself;

sentences.zh: 履薄臨淵，冀昭於元覽。

translations.literal: tread on thin ice and face the abyss, hoping to manifest in primal insight.
translations.idiomatic: walk on ice above an abyss, hoping the primal vision will clear.

sentences.zh: 兢兢栗栗，夙夜匪寧。

translations.literal: Trembling and fearful, restless day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful and uneasy, I find no rest by day or night.

sentences.zh: 及夫動干戈而必契靈誅，陳犧齋而克章善應，苟非天垂丕佑，神贊殊休，則安可致夷凶渠，就不戰之功，變沴戾氣，作有年之慶。

translations.literal: When mobilizing troops, divine punishment must be fulfilled; when offering sacrifices, good responses are manifest—without heaven’s great favor and the spirits’ singular blessing, how could we bring the barbarian ringleaders to ruin and achieve victory without battle, transform malignant qi into a year of abundance?
translations.idiomatic: When I take up arms Heaven’s judgment answers; when I offer sacrifice the good omen appears—without Heaven’s great aid and the spirits’ rare grace, how could traitor chiefs be levelled, victory won without battle, and foul air turned to a year of plenty?

sentences.zh: 況靈旗北指，喪犬羊於亂轍之間，飛騎西臨，下鄜、翟若走丸之易。

translations.literal: Moreover the spirit banners pointed north, scattering the dogs and sheep amid disorder; flying cavalry pressed west, taking Bin and Di as easily as rolling a pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit banners drove north and dogs and sheep fled in rout; flying columns pressed west and Bin and Di fell like a rolling ball.

sentences.zh: 息一隅之煙燧，復千里之封疆。

translations.literal: One corner’s beacon fires were quelled and a thousand li of territory restored.
translations.idiomatic: Beacon smoke in one quarter died and a thousand li of border returned.

sentences.zh: 而又掃蕩左馮，討除峴首。

translations.literal: Furthermore we swept Zuofeng and stormed Xianshou.
translations.idiomatic: We swept Zuofeng and stormed Xianshou as well.

sentences.zh: 故得外戎內夏，益知天命之攸歸，喙息蚑行，共識皇基之永固。

translations.literal: Thus outer barbarians and inner Chinese increasingly knew Heaven’s mandate had returned, and all who breathe and crawl recognized the imperial foundation would endure.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese alike saw that Heaven’s mandate had returned; every creature that breathes knew the throne would stand forever.

sentences.zh: 仰懷昭應，欲報無階。

translations.literal: Mindful of these manifest responses yet without means to repay,
translations.idiomatic: I cherish these signs yet have no way to repay them—

sentences.zh: 爰因南至之辰，親展圓丘之禮。

translations.literal: on this southern-extremity day I personally performed the round-altar rite.
translations.idiomatic: so on this day of the southern solstice I myself offered at the Round Altar.

sentences.zh: 茲惟大慶，必及下民，乃宏渙汗之私，以錫疲羸之幸。

translations.literal: This great celebration must reach the lower people; I spread this liberal bounty to grant fortune to the weary and weak.
translations.idiomatic: This great joy must reach the humble; I pour out grace to bless the tired and poor.

sentences.zh: 所冀漸增蘇息，亟致和平。

translations.literal: I hope gradually to increase relief and quickly attain peace.
translations.idiomatic: May relief grow little by little and peace come soon.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 朕自臨御以來，歲時尚邇，氛昏未殄，討伐猶頻。

translations.literal: Since taking the throne the years are still few, the murky air is not extinguished, and campaigns remain frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Since I began to rule the years are still short, the murk is not cleared, and war is still frequent.

sentences.zh: 甲兵須議於饋糧，飛挽頻勞於編戶，事非獲已，慮若納隍。

translations.literal: Armour and weapons require discussing rations; rapid transport repeatedly burdens registered households—this could not be avoided, my anxiety like drowning in a moat.
translations.idiomatic: Armies must be fed and relay convoys wear out the tax rolls—none of it could be helped; my heart is like a man drowning in a ditch.

sentences.zh: 宜所在長吏，倍切撫綏，明加勉諭，每官中抽差徭役，禁猾吏廣斂貪求。

translations.literal: Local senior officials everywhere should doubly strive to comfort and soothe, clearly encourage them, draw corvée laborers from each office in rotation, and forbid corrupt clerks from widening exactions and greedy demands,
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials everywhere must comfort the people twice over, urge them plainly, rotate corvée by office, and stop grasping clerks from extra levies and greed,

sentences.zh: 免至流散靡依，凋弊不濟。

translations.literal: lest the people scatter with nowhere to rely on and decline without recovery.
translations.idiomatic: lest families scatter homeless and the land sink beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 宜令河南府、開封府及諸道觀察使切加鈴轄，刺史、縣令不得因緣賦斂，分外擾人。

translations.literal: Henan and Kaifeng prefectures and all circuit observation commissioners should strictly supervise so prefects and magistrates may not use pretext of levying taxes to harass the people beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Henan, Kaifeng, and every observation commissioner must tighten control so prefects and magistrates cannot use tax pretexts to harass the people.

sentences.zh: 凡關庶獄，每望輕刑。

translations.literal: In all criminal cases I hope for lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In every criminal matter I look for lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 只候才罷用軍，必當便議優給。

translations.literal: Once military use ceases we shall promptly discuss generous grants.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies stand down we will at once consider generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 德音節文內有未該者，宜令所司類列條件奏聞。

translations.literal: Where the grace edict’s text is incomplete, the relevant offices should classify conditions and submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Where this grace edict is incomplete, let the offices list the gaps and report.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以羅周韓為天雄軍節度副使，知府事，從鄴王紹威病請也。

translations.literal: On jihai Luo Zhouhan was made vice military governor of Tianxiong and administered the prefecture, at Prince of Ye Shao Wei’s request due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Luo Zhouhan became vice military governor of Tianxiong and ran the prefecture at Prince of Ye Shao Wei’s plea of illness.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，幸穀水。

translations.literal: On xinchou he visited Gushui.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he went to Gushui.

sentences.zh: 戊午，禦文明殿，冊太傅張宗奭太保韓建受冊畢。

translations.literal: On wuwu the Emperor presided at Wuming Hall where Grand Tutor Zhang Zongshi and Grand Preceptor Han Jian completed receiving investiture seals.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu at Wuming Hall the investiture of Grand Tutor Zhang Zongshi and Grand Preceptor Han Jian was completed.

sentences.zh: 金吾仗引升輅車，儀仗導謁太廟訖，赴尚書省上。

translations.literal: The Golden Guard escorted them into the imperial carriage; the ceremonial guard led them to pay homage at the Imperial Ancestral Shrine, then they proceeded to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard led them to the imperial carriage; the guard of honor took them to the ancestral shrine and then to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 幸榆林坡閱兵，教諸都馬步兵。

translations.literal: He visited Yulin Slope to review troops and drill the various metropolitan horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Yulin Slope to review troops and drill the capital horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 敕改乾文院為文思院，行殿為興安殿，球場為興安球場，又改弓箭庫殿為宣武殿。

translations.literal: He ordered renaming Qianwen Academy to Wensi Academy, the traveling palace hall to Xing’an Hall, the ball ground to Xing’an Ball Ground, and the bow-and-arrow depot hall to Xuanwu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Qianwen Academy Wensi Academy, the traveling hall Xing’an Hall, the ball ground Xing’an Ball Ground, and the bow depot hall Xuanwu Hall.

sentences.zh: 靈州奏，鳳翔賊將劉知俊率邠、岐、秦、涇之師侵迫州城。

translations.literal: Lingzhou reported that Fengxiang rebel general Liu Zhijun led forces from Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing to press the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou reported that Fengxiang rebel Liu Zhijun led Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing troops against the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 帝遣陝州康懷英、華州寇彥卿率兵攻迫邠、寧，以緩朔方之寇。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Shaan Prefecture’s Kang Huaiying and Hua Prefecture’s Kou Yanqing to attack Bin and Ning to relieve pressure on Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Kang Huaiying of Shaan and Kou Yanqing of Hua to strike Bin and Ning and ease the Shuofang threat.

sentences.zh: 《五代春秋》：十一月，秦人來侵靈州。

translations.literal: 《Spring and Autumn of the Five Dynasties》: In the eleventh month Qin forces invaded Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 《Spring and Autumn of the Five Dynasties》 records: In the eleventh month Qin troops invaded Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 陝州康懷英侵秦，克甯、慶、衍三州。

translations.literal: Kang Huaiying of Shaan invaded Qin and captured Ning, Qing, and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaiying of Shaan attacked Qin and took Ning, Qing, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 秦人來襲，懷英兵敗於升平。

translations.literal: Qin forces counterattacked and Huaiying was defeated at Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: Qin struck back and Huaiying was beaten at Shengping.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙丑臘，較獵於甘泉驛。

translations.literal: On yichou of the twelfth month, the La solar term, he held a comparative hunt at Ganquan Post.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, La month of the twelfth month, he held a comparative hunt at Ganquan Post.

sentences.zh: 以蒲州肇跡之地，且因經略鄜、延，於是巡幸數月。

translations.literal: Because Puzhou was where the dynasty first rose and he was conducting operations toward Bin and Yan, he toured for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Puzhou was where the dynasty began and he was campaigning toward Bin and Yan, so he toured the region for months.

sentences.zh: 暇日游豫至焦梨店，頗述前事，念王重榮舊功，下詔褒獎而封崇之。

translations.literal: In leisure he traveled for pleasure to Jiaoli Shop and, recalling earlier events, thought of Wang Chongrong’s old achievements—he issued an edict of praise and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure he visited Jiaoli Shop, spoke of old days, and remembering Wang Chongrong’s service issued praise and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 國子監奏：「創造文宣王廟，仍請率在朝及天下現任官僚俸錢，每貫每月克一十五文，充土木之植。

translations.literal: The Directorate of the Imperial Academy memorialized: "We request construction of the Temple of King Wenxuan and ask that current and serving officials throughout the court and empire contribute fifteen cash per string of monthly salary for building materials.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy reported: "We will build the Temple of King Wenxuan and ask every serving official at court and in the provinces to give fifteen cash per string of monthly salary for timber and stone.

sentences.zh: 」允之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以所率官僚俸錢修文宣王廟。

translations.literal: That year the collected official salaries were used to repair the Temple of King Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the levied salaries went to repair the Temple of King Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 福建節度使王審知奏，舍錢造寺一所，請賜寺額。

translations.literal: Fujian military governor Wang Shenzhi memorialized offering funds to build a monastery and requesting a temple name.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhi, military governor of Fujian, offered money to build a monastery and asked for an imperial name.

sentences.zh: 敕名大樑萬歲之寺，仍許度僧四十九人。

translations.literal: It was named Monastery of Great Liang’s Myriad Years and forty-nine monks were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: It was named Monastery of Great Liang’s Myriad Years and forty-nine ordinations were allowed.

sentences.zh: 贈牢牆使王仁嗣司空，故同州押衙史肇右僕射，押衙王彥洪、高漢詮、丘奉言、仇瓊並刑部尚書，王筠御史司憲。

translations.literal: Posthumous honors were granted to detention commissioner Wang Rensi as grand master of splendid happiness, former Tong Prefecture escort guard Shi Zhao as right vice director, escort guards Wang Yanhong, Gao Hanchun, Qiu Fengyan, and Qiu Qiong each as minister of justice, and Wang Jun as censor-in-chief of the Bureau of Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rensi, detention commissioner, was posthumously made grand master of splendid happiness; Shi Zhao, former Tong escort guard, right vice director; Wang Yanhong, Gao Hanchun, Qiu Fengyan, and Qiu Qiong, escort guards, ministers of justice; Wang Jun, censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，知俊將叛，謀會諸將詢所宜，仁嗣等持正不撓，悉罹其酷，至是褒贈之。

translations.literal: When Zhijun was about to rebel he gathered the generals to consult; Rensi and others held firm and upright and all suffered cruelly—now they were posthumously rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhijun was plotting revolt he called the generals for counsel; Rensi and the rest stood firm and suffered cruelly—now they were honored in death.

sentences.zh: 劉守光上言，於薊州西與兄守文戰，擒守文。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang reported that west of Jizhou he battled his elder brother Shouwen and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang reported that west of Jizhou he fought his brother Shouwen and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 開平四年正月壬辰朔，帝御朝元殿，受百官稱賀，始用禮樂也。

translations.literal: On renchen, first day of the first month of Kaiping 4, the Emperor presided at Chaoyuan Hall, received congratulations from officials, and for the first time employed ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, New Year’s Day of Kaiping 4, the Emperor held Chaoyuan Hall, took the officials’ congratulations, and for the first time used court music.

sentences.zh: 敕：「公事難於稽遲，居處悉皆遙遠。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Public business is hard to delay in clearance and residences are all far away.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "State business cannot wait and homes are far away.

sentences.zh: 其逐日當直中書舍人及吏部司封知印郎官、少府監及篆印文兼書寫告身人吏等，並宜輪次於中書側近宿止。

translations.literal: Daily duty Secretariat draftsmen, Ministry of Personnel seal keepers, Directorate of the Palace Stores seal engravers and commission writers, and others should rotate lodging near the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Daily duty Secretariat draftsmen, Personnel seal clerks, Palace Stores seal-cutters and commission scribes, and the like should lodge in rotation near the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 」乙未，帝出師子門，至榆林坡下閱教。

translations.literal: " On yiwei the Emperor left Shizi Gate and went to Yulin Slope below to review drill.
translations.idiomatic: " On yiwei he left Shizi Gate and reviewed drill below Yulin Slope.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，幸保寧球場，錫宴宰臣及文武百官。

translations.literal: On renyin he visited Baoning Ball Ground and granted a feast to chief ministers and civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he went to Baoning Ball Ground and feasted chief ministers and the full establishment.

sentences.zh: 賜宰臣張宗奭已下分物有加，賜廣王分物。

translations.literal: He granted Zhang Zongshi and those below additional distributed goods and granted goods to the Prince of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhang Zongshi and those below extra shares and sent a share to the Prince of Guang.

sentences.zh: 及湖南開元寺禪長老可復號惠光大師，仍賜紫衣。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Hunan Kaiyuan Monastery Chan elder Ke Fu the religious name Hui Guang Great Master, with a purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Fu, Chan elder of Hunan’s Kaiyuan Monastery, was named Hui Guang Great Master and given a purple robe.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，幸甘水亭。

translations.literal: On yichou of the second month he visited Ganshui Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the second month he went to Ganshui Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 出師子門，幸榆林東北坡，教諸軍兵事。

translations.literal: He left Shizi Gate to Yulin northeast slope to drill the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He left Shizi Gate for the northeast slope of Yulin to drill the armies.

sentences.zh: 賜潞州投歸軍使張行恭錦服銀帶並食。

translations.literal: He granted Lu Prefecture defector military commissioner Zhang Xinggong brocade robes, a silver belt, and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xinggong, Lu defector and military commissioner, received brocade, a silver belt, and rations.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，宴于金鑾殿。

translations.literal: On wuchen he feasted at Jinluan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he held a feast at Jinluan Hall.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以春時無事，頻命宰臣勳戚宴于河南府池亭。

translations.literal: On jiaxu because spring was idle he frequently ordered chief ministers and meritorious kin to feast at Henan Prefecture pool pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, with a quiet spring, he often sent chief ministers and kinsmen of merit to feast at Henan’s pool pavilions.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，楊師厚赴鎮於陝。

translations.literal: On xinsi Yang Shihou departed for his post at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Yang Shihou left for his post at Shan.

sentences.zh: 寒食假，諸道節度使、郡守、勳臣競以春服賀。

translations.literal: During Cold Food leave, military governors, prefects, and meritorious ministers vied to present spring garments in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On Cold Food holiday governors, prefects, and men of merit competed to send spring garments in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 又連清明宴，以鞍轡馬及金銀器、羅錦進者迨千萬，乃禦宣威殿，宴宰臣及文武官四品已上。

translations.literal: Connected Clear and Bright feasts brought saddled horses and gold, silver, silks worth nearly ten million—then he presided at Xuanwei Hall and feasted chief ministers and officials of fourth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Clear and Bright season gifts of saddled horses, gold, silver, and silks neared ten million—then at Xuanwei Hall he feasted chief ministers and officials of fourth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 己丑，出光政門，至穀水觀麥。

translations.literal: On jichou he left Guangzheng Gate to Gushui to view the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he went out Guangzheng Gate to Gushui to see the wheat.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰，幸崇政院宴勳臣。

translations.literal: On renchen of the third month he visited Chongzheng Academy to feast meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the third month he feasted meritorious ministers at Chongzheng Academy.

sentences.zh: 己亥，幸天驥院宴侍臣。

translations.literal: On jihai he visited Tianji Academy to feast attendant ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he feasted attendant ministers at Tianji Academy.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，幸甘水亭宴宰臣、勳戚、翰林學士。

translations.literal: On renyin he visited Ganshui Pavilion to feast chief ministers, meritorious kin, and Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin at Ganshui Pavilion he feasted chief ministers, kinsmen of merit, and Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，宴宰臣於內殿。

translations.literal: On xinhai he feasted chief ministers in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he gave chief ministers a feast in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，于興安球場大饗六軍，樂春時也。

translations.literal: On bingchen at Xing’an Ball Ground he gave a great feast to the Six Armies, rejoicing in the spring season.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen at Xing’an Ball Ground he held a great feast for the Six Armies to celebrate spring.

sentences.zh: 四月壬戌，詔曰：「追養以祿，王者推歸厚之恩；

translations.literal: On renxu an edict stated: "Supporting parents with salary—kings extend the grace of returning kindness;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict read: "To support one’s parents from office salary is how a king repays deep kindness;

sentences.zh: 欲靜而風，人子抱終身之感。

translations.literal: wishing for stillness yet wind comes—a son bears lifelong feeling.
translations.idiomatic: to want peace yet feel the wind is a son’s lifelong debt."

sentences.zh: 其以刑部尚書致仕張策及三品、四品常參官二十二人先世，各追贈一等。

translations.literal: Retired Minister of Justice Zhang Ce and twenty-two regular attendees of third and fourth rank shall each have their forebears posthumously promoted one grade."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ce, retired minister of justice, and twenty-two third- and fourth-rank regular attendees shall each have one forebear raised a grade in posthumous rank."

sentences.zh: 」乙丑，宴崇政院。

translations.literal: On yichou he feasted at Chongzheng Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he feasted at Chongzheng Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝在籓及踐阼，勵精求理，深戒逸樂，未嘗命堂上歌舞。

translations.literal: When in the fief and upon taking the throne he strove in governance and deeply warned against pleasure—he never ordered song and dance on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: As prince and since taking the throne he had labored at rule and shunned dissipation—never once had he ordered hall music and dance.

sentences.zh: 是日，止令內妓升階，擊鼓弄曲甚歡，至午而罷。

translations.literal: That day he only had inner courtesans ascend the steps, beat drums and play tunes with great joy, ceasing at noon.
translations.idiomatic: That day he allowed only inner performers on the steps, drumming and playing in high spirits until noon.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，宋州節度使、衡王友諒進瑞麥，一莖三穗。

translations.literal: On dingmao Songzhou military governor, Prince of Heng You Liang, presented auspicious wheat with one stalk and three ears.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao You Liang, Prince of Heng and military governor of Songzhou, presented lucky wheat with three ears on one stalk.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：友諒獻瑞麥，帝曰：「豐年為上瑞，今宋州大水，安用此為！

translations.literal: 《Zizhi Tongjian》: You Liang presented auspicious wheat; the Emperor said: "A bountiful year is the supreme omen—now Songzhou has great flood, what use is this!
translations.idiomatic: 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: You Liang sent lucky wheat; the Emperor said, "A full harvest is the true omen—Songzhou is flooded; what is this for!

sentences.zh: 」詔除本縣令名，遣使詰責友諒。

translations.literal: An edict removed the county magistrate’s name and sent an envoy to reprimand You Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the county magistrate from the rolls and sent an envoy to rebuke You Liang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，幸建春門閱新樓，至七里屯觀麥，召從官食于樓。

translations.literal: On bingxu he visited Jianchun Gate to review the new tower, went to Qili Post to view wheat, and summoned attendant officials to eat at the tower.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he inspected the new tower at Jianchun Gate, went to Qili Post to see the wheat, and fed his attendants at the tower.

sentences.zh: 河南張昌孫及蒲、同主事吏賜物各有差。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsun of Henan and clerks in charge at Pu and Tong were granted goods in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsun of Henan and the lead clerks at Pu and Tong received graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 帝過朝邑，見鎮將位在縣令上，問左右，或對曰：「宿官秩高。

translations.literal: Passing Chaoyi he saw the garrison commander seated above the county magistrate and asked those nearby; some answered: "The veteran office ranks higher."
translations.idiomatic: At Chaoyi he saw the garrison commander seated above the magistrate and asked why; someone said the old post outranked the new.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「令長字人也，鎮使捕盜耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Magistrates nurture the people; garrison commanders only catch bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "A magistrate raises the people; a garrison chief only catches thieves.

sentences.zh: 且鎮將多是邑民，奈何得居民父母上，是無禮也。

translations.literal: Moreover most garrison commanders are natives of the locality—how can they stand above the people’s parents? This is without propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Most garrison chiefs are local men—how can they sit above the people’s parents? That is rank without rite."

sentences.zh: 」至是，敕天下鎮使，官秩無高卑，位在邑令下。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict directed that throughout the realm garrison commanders, regardless of rank high or low, should stand below the county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then placed every garrison commander, high or low, below the county magistrate throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 葉縣鎮遏使馮德武于蔡州西平縣界殺戮山賊，擒首領張濆等七人以獻。

translations.literal: Ye County suppression commissioner Feng Dewu at the boundary of Xiping County of Cai Prefecture killed mountain bandits and presented the seven leaders including Zhang Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dewu, Ye County suppression commissioner, killed mountain bandits on the Xiping border in Cai and sent up seven chiefs including Zhang Fen.

sentences.zh: 鎮海軍節度使錢鏐擊高灃於湖州，大敗之，梟夷擒殺萬人，拔其郡，湖州平。

translations.literal: Zhenhai military governor Qian Liu attacked Gao Hong at Huzhou, routed him greatly, beheaded and captured ten thousand, took the prefecture—Huzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu of Zhenhai attacked Gao Hong at Huzhou, crushed him, killed or captured ten thousand men, and took the city; Huzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 先是，灃以州叛入淮南，故詔鏐討之也。

translations.literal: Previously Hong had rebelled with the prefecture and entered Huainan, therefore the edict ordered Liu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had earlier rebelled and gone over to Huainan, which was why Liu was ordered to strike him.

sentences.zh: 五月己丑朔，以連雨不止，至壬辰，禦文明殿，命宰臣分拜祠廟。

translations.literal: On jichou, first day of the fifth month, because rain continued unceasing, until renchen the Emperor presided at Wuming Hall and ordered chief ministers to separately worship at shrines and temples.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the first of the fifth month, rain would not stop; by renchen the Emperor was at Wuming Hall and sent chief ministers to sacrifice at separate shrines.

sentences.zh: 自朔旦至癸巳，內外以午日奉獻巨萬，計馬三千蹄，餘稱是，復相率助修內壘。

translations.literal: From the first dawn to guisi, within and without presented on the noon festival gifts in the tens of thousands, counting three thousand horse hooves, the rest in proportion, and again jointly assisted in repairing the inner ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: From New Year’s dawn to guisi, court and provinces gave Midyear gifts by the tens of thousands—three thousand horses among them—and again joined to repair the inner walls.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔曰：「奇邪亂正，假偽奪真，既刑典之不容，宜違犯而勿赦。

translations.literal: On jiachen an edict stated: "Strange and evil disorder the correct, falsehood seizes the genuine—since the penal code does not permit it, violators should not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen an edict said: "The crooked overturn the straight and fakes drive out truth—law forbids it and offenders must not be spared.

sentences.zh: 應東、西兩京及諸道州府，創造假犀玉真珠腰帶、璧珥並諸色售用等，一切禁斷，不得更造作。

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Capitals and all circuit prefectures—counterfeit rhinoceros horn, jade, pearl waist belts, ear ornaments, and all colored goods for sale—everything is forbidden and may not be further manufactured.
translations.idiomatic: In both capitals and every prefecture, fake rhinoceros, jade, pearl belts, earrings, and painted goods for sale are banned and may not be made again.

sentences.zh: 如公私人家先已有者，所在送納長吏，對面毀棄；

translations.literal: If private households already possess them, deliver them to the senior official locally to be destroyed face to face;
translations.idiomatic: Households that already own them must surrender them to the local chief for destruction on the spot;

sentences.zh: 如行敕後有人故違，必當極法。

translations.literal: if after the edict someone deliberately violates, capital punishment will certainly be applied.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who defies the edict will face the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 仍委所在州府差人檢察收捕，明行處斷。

translations.literal: Still entrust each prefecture to dispatch persons to inspect, seize, and explicitly execute punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture must send men to search, seize, and punish openly."

sentences.zh: 」魏博節度使、守太師、兼中書令、鄴王羅紹威薨，帝哀慟曰：「天不使我一海內，何奪忠臣之速也！

translations.literal: Weibo military governor, regent grand preceptor, concurrent director of the Secretariat and Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei died; the Emperor mourned greatly: "Heaven does not let me have all within the seas—why take a loyal minister so soon!
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei, Prince of Ye, regent grand preceptor, director of the Secretariat, and military governor of Weibo, died; the Emperor grieved: "Heaven will not let me unite the realm—why take a loyal minister so soon!

sentences.zh: 」詔贈尚書令。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六月己未朔，詔軍鎮勿起土功。

translations.literal: On jiwei, first day of the sixth month, an edict directed military garrisons not to undertake earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the first of the sixth month, garrisons were forbidden to begin earthworks.

sentences.zh: 七月壬子，宴宰臣、河南尹、翰林學士、兩街使于甘水亭。

translations.literal: On renzi he feasted chief ministers, Henan prefect, Hanlin academicians, and commissioners of both streets at Ganshui Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he feasted chief ministers, the Henan prefect, Hanlin scholars, and both street commissioners at Ganshui Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，宴群臣于宣威殿，賜物有差。

translations.literal: On bingchen he feasted the officials at Xuanwei Hall and granted goods in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen at Xuanwei Hall he feasted the officials and gave graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊攻逼夏州。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun pressed Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun pressed Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：七月，岐王與邠涇二帥各遣使告晉，請合兵攻定難節度使李仁福，晉王遣振武節度使周德威將兵會之，合五萬眾，圍夏州。

translations.literal: 《Zizhi Tongjian》: In the seventh month the Prince of Qi and the military governors of Bin and Jing each sent envoys to report to Jin, requesting combined armies to attack Dingnan military governor Li Renfu; the Prince of Jin sent Zhenwu military governor Zhou Dewei to lead troops to join them—altogether fifty thousand, besieging Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: In the seventh month the Prince of Qi and the Bin and Jing governors asked Jin for a joint attack on Li Renfu of Dingnan; the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu with fifty thousand men to besiege Xia.

sentences.zh: 以宣化軍留後李思安為東北面行營都指揮使，陝州節度使楊師厚為西路行營招討使。

translations.literal: Xuanhua army acting prefect Li Si’an was made commander-in-chief of the northeast campaign army; Shanzhou military governor Yang Shihou was made suppression commissioner of the western-route campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si’an, acting prefect of Xuanhua, became northeast campaign commander-in-chief; Yang Shihou of Shan became western-route suppression commissioner.

sentences.zh: 福州貢方物，獻桐皮扇，廣州貢犀玉，獻舶上薔薇水。

translations.literal: Fuzhou presented regional products with paulownia-bark fans; Guangzhou presented rhinoceros horn and jade with shipborne rose water.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou sent tribute of paulownia-bark fans; Guangzhou sent rhinoceros, jade, and rose water from the ships.

sentences.zh: 時陳、許、汝、蔡、潁五州境內有蝝為災，俄而許州上言，有野禽群飛蔽空，旬日之間，食蝝皆盡，是歲乃大有秋。

translations.literal: At that time within Chen, Xu, Ru, Cai, and Ying five prefectures caterpillars brought disaster; soon Xuzhou reported wild birds flocking and covering the sky—in ten days they ate all caterpillars, and that year brought great autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Caterpillars ravaged Chen, Xu, Ru, Cai, and Ying; then Xuzhou reported birds darkening the sky—in ten days the worms were gone and the year brought a rich harvest.

sentences.zh: 八月，車駕西征。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the imperial carriage campaigned west.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Emperor marched west.

sentences.zh: 己巳，次陝府。

translations.literal: On jisi he halted at Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he stopped at Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時憫雨，且命宰臣從官分禱靈跡，日中而雨，翼日止，帝大悅。

translations.literal: At this time pitying the rain, he also ordered chief ministers and attendant officials to separately pray at numinous sites; at midday rain came, next day it ceased—the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the rains, he sent chief ministers and attendants to pray at holy sites; rain fell at noon and stopped the next day—the Emperor rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 辛未，老人星見。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Old Man star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Old Man star appeared.

sentences.zh: 是日，宴本府節度使楊師厚及扈從官於行宮，賜師厚帛千匹，仍授西路行營招討使。

translations.literal: That day he feasted this prefecture’s military governor Yang Shihou and attendant officials at the traveling palace, granted Shihou one thousand bolts of silk, and again appointed western-route campaign suppression commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That day at the traveling palace he feasted Yang Shihou and the entourage, gave Shihou a thousand bolts of silk, and confirmed him western-route suppression commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙子，宴文武從官軍使已下，設龜茲樂，賜物有差。

translations.literal: On bingzi he feasted civil and military attendant officials and army commissioners below, set out Kuche music, and granted goods in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he feasted civil and military attendants and army commissioners, played Kuche music, and gave graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 九月丁亥朔，命宰臣於兢赴西都，祀昊天上帝於圓丘。

translations.literal: On dinghai, first day of the ninth month, he ordered chief minister Yu Jing to go to the Western Capital to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord at the Round Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the first of the ninth month, he sent chief minister Yu Jing to the Western Capital to offer at the Round Altar to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 甲午，至西京。

translations.literal: On jiawu he reached the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he reached the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：

translations.literal: He issued an edict stating:
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 朕聞歷代帝王，首推堯、舜；

translations.literal: I have heard that among successive emperors and kings, Yao and Shun are foremost;
translations.idiomatic: I am told that of all emperors and kings, Yao and Shun stand first;

sentences.zh: 為人父母，孰比禹、湯。

translations.literal: as parents of the people, who compare with Yu and Tang?
translations.idiomatic: and as fathers and mothers of the people, none match Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 睿謀高出於古先，聖德普聞于天下，尚或卑躬待士，屈己求賢。

translations.literal: Their wise designs surpassed antiquity and sagely virtue was universally heard in the realm—yet they still humbled themselves to await scholars and bent themselves to seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Their wisdom outran the ancients and their virtue filled the world—yet they still humbled themselves for scholars and stooped to find talent.

sentences.zh: 俯仰星雲，慮一民之遺逸；

translations.literal: Looking up and down at the stars and clouds, they worried over one subject gone astray;
translations.idiomatic: They scanned heaven and earth, fearing even one man was lost;

sentences.zh: 網羅岩穴，恐片善之韜藏。

translations.literal: casting nets over cliffs and caves, they feared a single goodness concealed.
translations.idiomatic: they cast nets over crags and caves, lest one virtue stay hidden.

sentences.zh: 延爵祿以徵求，設丹青而訪召，使其為政，樂在進賢，蓋由國有萬幾，朝稱百揆，非才不治，得士則昌。

translations.literal: They extended ranks and salaries to summon, set up portraits to call forth—making those who govern delight in advancing the worthy; for the state has ten thousand affairs and the court a hundred duties—not talent and there is no order; gain men and there is prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: They raised rank and pay to call men in and hung portraits to invite them—so rulers loved to advance the able; a state has a thousand tasks and a court a hundred posts—without talent nothing is governed, with men it flourishes.

sentences.zh: 自朕光宅中區，迄今三載，宵分輟寐，日旰忘餐，思共力於廟謀，庶永清于王道。

translations.literal: Since I have illumined the central land until now three years, at midnight I cease sleep, at sundown I forget meals, thinking to join strength in temple counsel, hoping ever to clear the royal way.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the central land three years have passed—I sleep little at midnight and miss meals at dusk, seeking counsel in the ancestral hall and a clear royal road.

sentences.zh: 而乃朝廷之內，或未盡於昌言；

translations.literal: Yet within the court perhaps forthright speech is not exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in court frank speech may not be fully heard;

sentences.zh: 軍旅之間，亦罕聞於奇策。

translations.literal: within the armies also rarely is marvelous strategy heard.
translations.idiomatic: in the armies bold plans are seldom offered.

sentences.zh: 眷言方嶽，下及山林，豈無英奇，副我延佇。

translations.literal: Turning my thoughts to regional governors down to mountain forests—is there not excellence to meet my long waiting?
translations.idiomatic: I turn from the governors to the mountains—is there no excellence to end my long waiting?

sentences.zh: 諸道都督、觀察防禦使等，或勳高翊世，或才號知人，必於途巷之賢，備察芻蕘之士。

translations.literal: Military governors, observation and defense commissioners, and the like—whether merit high enough to assist the age or talent renowned for knowing men—must among lane-and-alley worthies thoroughly observe hay-and-wood scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Governors, observation and defense commissioners—whether your merit supports the age or your fame is for knowing men—search lanes and huts and heed the counsel of the humble.

sentences.zh: 詔到，可精搜郡邑，博訪賢良，喻之以千載一時，約之以高官美秩，諒無求備，惟在得人。

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, meticulously search counties and cities, broadly visit the good and able, persuade them with this once-in-a-thousand-years moment, bind them with high office and fine rank—surely do not seek completeness, only gain men.
translations.idiomatic: When this edict arrives, search counties and towns, seek the good and able, tell them the age comes once in a thousand years, promise high office and rich rank—do not demand perfection, only find men.

sentences.zh: 如有卓犖不羈，沉潛自負，通霸王之上略，達文武之大綱，究古今刑政之源，識禮樂質文之變，朕則待之不次，委以非常，用佐經綸，豈勞階級。

translations.literal: If there is surpassing excellence unrestrained, submerged self-confidence, penetrating the supreme stratagems of hegemons and kings, mastering the great outlines of civil and military affairs, investigating the sources of punishment and government ancient and modern, understanding the transformations of ritual and music substance and ornament—I shall treat them out of order and entrust them extraordinarily to assist in governance—why trouble with grades?
translations.idiomatic: If a man is wholly outstanding, self-contained, master of kingly strategy, versed in civil and military outline, deep in law old and new, skilled in ritual’s form and substance—I will use him out of turn and set him at my side without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 如或一言拔俗，一事出群，亦當舍短從長，隨才授任。

translations.literal: If one statement lifts above custom or one affair stands out from the crowd, also set aside the short and follow the long, assign office according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: If one word rises above the common or one deed stands out, overlook small faults, use the long gift, and appoint by talent.

sentences.zh: 大小方圓之器，寧限九流，溫良恭儉之人，難誣十室。

translations.literal: Vessels great and small, square and round—can the nine streams be limited? Gentle, good, respectful, frugal men—the ten-household hamlet is hard to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Great vessels and small, square and round—can the nine currents be bounded? Good and gentle men are not hidden in a hamlet of ten houses.

sentences.zh: 勉思薦舉，勿至因循，俟爾發揚，慰予翹渴。

translations.literal: Strive to think of recommendation, do not delay—await your flourishing, comfort my eager thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Recommend with zeal, do not delay—lift up what you find and quench my thirst.

sentences.zh: 仍從別敕處分。

translations.literal: Still follow separate edict disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Further rules follow in a separate edict.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以久雨，命宰臣薛貽矩抃定鼎門，趙光逢祠嵩嶽。

translations.literal: On xinchou, because of long rain, he ordered chief ministers Xue Yiju to worship at Dingding Gate and Zhao Guangfeng at Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, with rain unending, he sent Xue Yiju to worship at Dingding Gate and Zhao Guangfeng to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 敕：「魏博管內刺史，比來州務，並委督郵。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Weibo prefectural military governors—lately prefectural affairs have all been delegated to supervisory commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "In Weibo, prefects lately leave all business to supervisory commissioners.

sentences.zh: 遂使曹官擅其威權，州牧同於閑冗，俾循通制，宜塞異端。

translations.literal: Thus petty officials usurp their authority and prefects are like idle supernumeraries—to follow the universal system, irregular paths should be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Petty clerks seize power and prefects sit idle—to restore the common rule, shut off side paths.

sentences.zh: 並依河南諸州例，刺史得以專達。

translations.literal: All shall follow the example of Henan prefectures—prefects may report directly."
translations.idiomatic: Follow Henan: prefects may report directly to court."

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，頒奪馬令。

translations.literal: On renyin the horse-seizure edict was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the edict seizing war horses was issued.

sentences.zh: 先是，王師擊賊，獲馬多上獻，至是盡止之，蓋欲邀其奮擊之功也。

translations.literal: Previously when the royal army struck rebels, captured horses were mostly presented upward—now all was stopped, intending to invite their fierce striking merit.
translations.idiomatic: Before, horses taken in rebel fights were mostly sent up as tribute—now that stopped, so men would fight all the harder.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，王師敗蕃寇于夏州。

translations.literal: On yisi the royal army defeated the barbarian bandits at Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the imperial army beat the barbarian rebels at Xia.

sentences.zh: 初，劉知俊誘沙陀振武賊帥周德威、涇原賊帥李繼鸞合步騎五萬大舉，欲俯拾夏台，節度使李仁福兵力俱乏，以急來告。

translations.literal: Initially Liu Zhijun induced Shatuo Zhenwu rebel leader Zhou Dewei and Jingyuan rebel leader Li Jiluan to combine infantry and cavalry fifty thousand in a great advance, intending to pick up Xia Terrace easily; military governor Li Renfu’s strength was entirely lacking and he reported in urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun had drawn Shatuo Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu and Li Jiluan of Jingyuan with fifty thousand horse and foot, thinking Xia would fall at a touch; Li Renfu was spent and cried for help.

sentences.zh: 先是，供奉官張漢玫宣諭在壁，國禮使杜廷隱賜幣于夏，及石堡寨，聞賊至，以防卒三百人馳入州。

translations.literal: Previously duty commissioner Zhang Hanmei had proclaimed at the wall; state rites commissioner Du Tingyin had bestowed gifts at Xia, and at Shibao Stockade heard bandits coming and with three hundred defense soldiers galloped into the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Hanmei, duty commissioner, was at the walls; Du Tingyin, state rites envoy, was gifting at Xia—at Shibao Stockade they heard the enemy and rode in with three hundred guards.

sentences.zh: 既而大兵圍合，廷隱、漢玫與指揮使張初、李君用率州民防卒，與仁福部分固守，晝夜戮力逾月。

translations.literal: Soon the great army surrounded; Tingyin, Hanmei, commanders Zhang Chu and Li Junyong with prefectural people and defense soldiers, with Renfu dividing defense, strove day and night for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: The host soon encircled the city; Tingyin, Hanmei, Zhang Chu, Li Junyong, militia and garrison fought with Renfu for more than a month without rest.

sentences.zh: 及鄜、延援至，大軍奮擊，敗之。

translations.literal: When Bin and Yan relief arrived, the great army struck fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin and Yan relief came, the imperial army struck and broke them.

sentences.zh: 河東、邠、岐賊分路逃遁，夏州圍解。

translations.literal: Hedong, Bin, and Qi rebels fled by separate routes; Xia Prefecture siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, Bin, and Qi rebels fled apart and the siege of Xia was raised.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：甲申，遣夾馬指揮使李遇、劉綰自鄜、延趨銀、夏。

translations.literal: 《Zizhi Tongjian》: On jiashen he dispatched flank-horse commanders Li Yu and Liu Chao from Bin and Yan toward Yin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: On jiashen he sent flank-horse commanders Li Yu and Liu Chao from Bin and Yan toward Yin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 李遇等至夏州，岐、晉兵皆解去。

translations.literal: When Li Yu and others reached Xia Prefecture, Qi and Jin armies all dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu reached Xia, Qi and Jin troops all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔曰：「劉知俊貴為方伯，尊極郡王，而乃背誕朝恩，竄投賊壘，固神人之共怒，諒天地所不容。

translations.literal: On bingwu an edict stated: "Liu Zhijun was ennobled as regional governor, exalted to prince of a command—yet he betrayed court grace and fled to the rebel camp; surely gods and men jointly rage and Heaven and Earth cannot contain him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu an edict said: "Liu Zhijun was made governor and raised to prince—yet he betrayed the court and fled to rebels; gods and men alike rage and heaven and earth will not hold him.

sentences.zh: 雖命討除，尚稽擒戮，宜懸爵賞，以大功名，必有忠貞，咸思憤發。

translations.literal: Though ordered for suppression, capture and slaughter are still delayed—suspended ranks and rewards should magnify achievement—there must be the loyal and steadfast who all think to blaze with anger.
translations.idiomatic: Though we ordered his destruction, he still lives—hang out rank and gold to swell merit; let every loyal man burn to strike.

sentences.zh: 有生擒劉知俊者，賞錢千萬，授節度使，首級次之；

translations.literal: Whoever captures Liu Zhijun alive—reward ten million cash, appoint military governor; head next in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever takes Zhijun alive gets ten million cash and a military governorship; for his head, the next reward;

sentences.zh: 得孟審登者，錢百萬，除刺史；

translations.literal: whoever gets Meng Shendeng—one million cash, appoint prefect;
translations.idiomatic: for Meng Shendeng, one million and a prefecture;

sentences.zh: 得孫亢、卓環、劉儒、張鄰等，賞有差。

translations.literal: whoever gets Sun Kang, Zhuo Huan, Liu Ru, Zhang Lin, and others—rewards in varying amounts."
translations.idiomatic: for Sun Kang, Zhuo Huan, Liu Ru, Zhang Lin, and the rest, graded rewards."

sentences.zh: 」乙卯，宴會群臣于宣威殿。

translations.literal: On yimao he feasted the officials at Xuanwei Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he feasted the officials at Xuanwei Hall.
